brief: A podcast player where episodes are constellations — listened ones glow, series form patterns

dominant_strengths: Strong metaphor: glowing constellations as series creates immediate emotional resonance and a memorable visual identity for browsing episodes
Cohesive purple-to-black gradient with warm yellow stars produces excellent atmospheric color harmony and dimensional depth
Legend card and now-playing bar use restrained typography hierarchy that doesn't fight the celestial canvas
dominant_weaknesses: Constellations lack labels, hover affordances, or any visible mapping between a star and an actual episode — pure aesthetic, no wayfinding
Vast empty center wastes screen real estate; star clusters drift without compositional anchoring or clear reading path
No visible search, filtering, queue, or progress-on-star indicators — behavioral utility collapses beneath the metaphor
fix_priorities: Add hover/focus states on stars revealing episode title, duration, and progress ring to make the metaphor functional
Introduce subtle constellation labels (series names) and a 'currently playing' pulse to anchor navigation
Tighten composition with intentional star placement so constellations feel authored, not randomly scattered
Provide a secondary list/grid toggle for users who need to scan rather than explore
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral and reflective dominate through poetic metaphor, but behavioral usability is severely undercooked with no clear interaction model.
rationale.intent_fit: Captures the constellation concept beautifully at the surface, yet stops short of resolving how listening states actually drive the patterns into a usable library.
